## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pāṭihāriyakathā* ("Discussion of Demonstrations") is a treatise in the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, situated within the Khuddaka Nikāya of the Pali Tipiṭaka [Hazra 1994]. Formally enumerated among the thirty treatises forming the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, the text adopts an analytical, Abhidhamma-style exposition of themes inherited from the early discourses [Hazra 1994]. Specifically, it elaborates upon the classical threefold classification of marvels or demonstrations: the miracle of psychic potency (*iddhi* or *iddhipāṭihāriya*), the marvel of thought-reading or telepathic discernment (*ādesanā*), and the superior marvel of pedagogical instruction (*anusāsanī*) [Hazra 1994].
